items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: And Sidney Bechet, he was playing clarinet with us, you see.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. He told that funny story about him being on the Smoky Mary. Tell us about it.

We used to play at Millenburg for picnics out there. Those were only picnics. And Sidney Bechet, he was playing clarinet with us, you see. And well, and Manuel Perez was playing trumpet. And we had the same fella Jimmy Pollard playing violin too. He used to play with his two over there. And we'd play them picnics. Cause we used to take a man when needed a man on the picnic. We'd have extra man when needed, you see. And Sidney Bechet would get on that old Smoky Mary, you know, that running out the Millenburg and…
Well, speaking of that term Dixieland, I never did ask fast either. When the word jazz began being used here in New Orleans, can you remember?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Yeah, Bichet was good, yeah, but he was better.

ctx.x: Where did he die? The clarinet play, is that the one that went up north or stayed here?

Oh, that fellow, that fellow was a famous musician. Was he from a musical family, or? He from, he from, he didn't have much, much kin, folks there, but he was a great, great, great saxophone and clarinet. Uh, yeah, but I'm trying to think of what he did, no. Could he read much, or? Could he? Ha! Sight reader. A man could read. If he hear a number playin, and he had a shirt with a cuff on it, he, he, he, he'd ride it all right, right on his cuff. Was he as good as Bichet, or T.O., or any of those people? Well,…
Did you know Charlie? He played with all of us. Hmm? He played with all of us. Yeah. Uh huh. What about Charlie Galloway? Did you know him? Charlie Galloway, I worked with, uh,

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: No, we had, we had, he's dead now. We had a baby, Bayshake, Sidney Bayshake.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. Was it a pic on that same gap with you, Willie?
No, we had, we had, he's dead now. We had a baby, Bayshake, Sidney Bayshake. Oh, yeah.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: He's dead now. I'm trying to think his name off. Y'all know him good, too. He died up in a parish somewhere up in France.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. I thought you said there was a little dog fellow there on clarinet at one time.

Well, he did have me meet you. He's dead now. I'm trying to think his name off. Y'all know him good, too. He died up in a parish somewhere up in France. You mean Sidney Bichet? Sidney Bichet. Sidney Bichet.
And you said he was about to bash tail on there earlier.
